newsitem.title: USA: Calif. transmission operator, pool start-up okayed.
newsitem.headline: Calif. transmission operator, pool start-up okayed.

text.p: California Public Utilities Commission Tuesday approved access to funding for an independent system operator and power exchange to help facilitate the move to open competition in the state.
The order allows boards of operator and exchange unconditional access to $250 million set aside in August for hardware and software systems.
Federal approval of the operator and exchange rates is pending.

Under California's plan to phase-in competition in the electricity industry from 1998, the operator will control and operate the state's electric transmission system. The exchange will pool electricity from producers and post prices.
Currently, individual utilities own and operate the transmission lines and retail power prices are determined by CPUC based on utility costs.
The Commission said it ordered utilities to execute necessary trust agreements within the next 10 days.
